support_josh: Heads up — Customer (liz@brightline) reports embeddings v1 throughput down ~3x after last infra deploy. tokens/sec steady, vectors/sec dropped. payload dim still 1536. No schema changes. Attaching a short repro and logs.

sre_ash: :eyes: Can you paste a sample request_id and an example curl? Also which model variant? quantized/float?

support_josh: request_id=rq_20260315_8f9a, model=redwood-emb-1536-quant. Example curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-emb-1536-quant","input":["a","b","c","d"]}'
```
Vectors/sec observed: ~40k -> ~13k after deploy. Tokens/sec roughly unchanged.

devon_dev: Any 429s or auth spikes? Could be batching or kvcache backpressure.

support_josh: No 401/403. There are 429 spikes in the serving logs but with reason "gpu_queue_wait" not auth. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] rq_20260315_8f9a INFO batch_size=4 gpu_queue_wait_ms=312 kvcache_wait_ms=4
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] rq_20260315_8f9a WARN per_token_latency_ms=2.8 vectors_generated=4
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] rq_20260315_8f9a DEBUG queue_depth=27 gpu_slots_busy=96/100
```

maria_infra: This looks like GPU slot saturation + queue depth. Recent infra deploy bumped max_concurrent_batches from 8 -> 12 and changed batching window heuristic. Could cause pathological small-batch padding on mixed payload sizes.

devon_dev: Repro suggestion: run a fixed-dim bulk test to compare continuous stream vs burst. I spun a quick load locally:
```
python perf_repro.py --model redwood-emb-1536-quant --concurrency 40 --batch-window-ms 20 --inputs 10000
```
Result: tokens/sec unchanged, vectors/sec drops when batch-window < 30ms and when autoscale doesn't allocate extra slots.

sre_ash: Good hint. Also check kvcache eviction/lock contention — small payloads cause more batches and KV locks. ops-bot, can you pull kube events for the pool for 14:00-14:10?

ops-bot: kube events pulled for pool emb-prod-quant (14:00-14:10) — autoscaler fired +2 nodes at 14:03, but scheduling delay ~45s. Several pods showed CPU pressure and OOMKilled=false. Summary: node add lag might have caused GPU queueing.

support_josh: Customer reported they send mixed array lengths (1-256 tokens). Might be thundering herd of short vectors. They were previously using legacy batching profile.

maria_infra: Two mitigation paths: 1) rollback batching heuristic change to keep max_concurrent_batches=8 until we tune; 2) enable per-customer small-batch flattening (force batch_repack) — temporary toggle available behind /admin flag.

devon_dev: Also try a quick workaround for customer: set request header X-Redwood-Batch-Mode: small-batch to disable aggressive packing. Could buy time while infra tunes.

support_josh: Sent workaround to customer, they confirmed slight improvement: vectors/sec ~18k now (still below old 40k). They will run our perf script and share results shortly.

sre_ash: Next steps: (a) collect more rq_ids from customer for end-to-end traces, (b) revert heuristic in canary and run synthetic load, (c) instrument kvcache lock latencies more aggressively. I'll open a rollout revert PR if repro matches.

support_josh: Thanks all. Adding customer_liz to thread for visibility. :thumbsup:

customer_liz: Thanks team — will attach perf.csv and a short timeline. Appreciate the quick workaround.
